environment.description: EKS pod in namespace 'platform-tools' with a custom seccomp profile loaded via the node's /var/lib/kubelet/seccomp/profiles/diagnostics-restricted.json. The profile uses SCMP_ACT_ERRNO as defaultAction with an explicit allowlist of syscalls. The profile permits read, write, openat, close, fstat, mmap, mprotect, brk, rt_sigaction, rt_sigprocmask, ioctl, access, getpid, clone (for threads only via SCMP_CMP_MASKED_EQ on flags), futex, epoll_wait, epoll_ctl, accept4, bind, listen, getsockname, recvmsg, sendmsg, and clock_gettime. Critically, execve, execveat, fork, vfork, ptrace, and the clone syscall without CLONE_THREAD flag are NOT in the allowlist and return EPERM. The pod annotation is: seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/pod: localhost/profiles/diagnostics-restricted.json (legacy) AND spec.securityContext.seccompProfile.type: Localhost with localhostProfile: profiles/diagnostics-restricted.json. The Python process itself runs (it was exec'd at container start by the container runtime before the seccomp filter was applied via the OCI runtime spec), but any subprocess.run() call with shell=True will fail because /bin/sh cannot be execve'd.

config.network_policy: allow ingress from namespace platform-tools only
config.note: Python interpreter is started by container entrypoint before seccomp filter is applied by OCI runtime hook at container start
